_provenance.note: Third real paper end-to-end (Epic AI): Gibbs & Candes (2021), 'Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift' (NeurIPS 2021), lifted from prose into a grounded dgroup by an in-session Claude Code sub-agent (no API call), in the style of Epic K (arXiv 2006.06138) and Epic V (Nesterov). This paper is special: the system had already PREDICTED its existence. Conjecture C6 (Epic AF), judged plausible, projected across the online_gradient_descent ~~ weighted-conformal analogy that 'the weighted conformal calibration procedure is a no-regret play'. ACI is exactly that result in the real literature: it runs an online gradient update on the miscoverage level (alpha_{t+1} = alpha_t + gamma*(alpha - err_t)), a no-regret procedure with bounded {0,1} gradient feedback, which restores long-run coverage under ARBITRARY distribution shift. So its set-cover decomposition should read it as a genuine CROSS-FIELD synthesis: borrowed online no-regret machinery + borrowed conformal-set machinery + a novel residual that is precisely the NO_REGRET -> COVERAGE bridge (plus its distribution-shift robustness) that neither field alone provides. Grounded; every symbol is a verbatim substring of its statement, checked by grounding.verify.

target.name: adaptive_conformal_inference
target.text: Adaptive conformal inference builds a conformal prediction set from nonconformity scores, then updates the miscoverage level with an online update driven by bounded gradient feedback from the coverage errors, a no-regret online procedure over the rounds; because the no-regret online procedure controls the long-run miscoverage, the conformal prediction set attains marginal coverage at the target level even under arbitrary distribution shift.
